Tense is the form of a verb that shows the time of an action, that is, when something happens. There are three main tenses: (1) Present tense - action happening now, e.g. 'I eat'. (2) Past tense - action that has already happened, e.g. 'I ate'. (3) Future tense - action that will happen later, e.g. 'I will eat'. So the verb changes to show whether you are talking about now, before, or later.

Change to past tense: Emeka plays football every evening.

To change to the past tense, we change the verb 'plays' to its past form. The past tense of 'play' is 'played'. We also drop 'every evening' or change it to show past time if needed. So the sentence becomes: 'Emeka played football.' (You could add 'yesterday evening' to make the time clear: 'Emeka played football yesterday evening.')

What is the difference between 'I write' and 'I am writing'?

Both are in the present, but they are different forms. 'I write' is the simple present tense; it shows a habit or something done regularly, e.g. 'I write a letter to my uncle every month.' 'I am writing' is the present continuous tense; it shows an action happening right now, e.g. 'Be quiet, I am writing my note at this moment.' So use the simple present for habits and the present continuous for actions in progress now.
